releases.title: collectZ v3.29.8
releases.summary: Adds durable, non-mutating review decisions for individual BookOrbit and Kavita metadata differences, so provider evidence can be approved, rejected, or deferred before any future apply policy exists.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added an append-only, exact-library-scoped review ledger tied to the canonical media record and immutable provider observation.
Binds each decision to server-computed observation and current-value fingerprints so changed canonical data makes an earlier decision visibly outdated.
Adds approve, reject, and seven-day defer actions to Library Provider history.
Returns only the latest safe review projection; internal actor and ownership identifiers remain private.
Rejects attempts to review unsupported, matching, absent, or no-longer-current differences.
Extended OpenAPI, migration inventory, provider contract, unit/source checks, and the BookOrbit runtime smoke.

releases.title: collectZ v3.29.7
releases.summary: Makes immutable BookOrbit and Kavita evidence easier to review by showing how allowlisted observed bibliographic facts compare with the current canonical record, without applying metadata or changing provider authority.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a derived comparison to each workspace-authorized provider observation readback.
Compares an explicit allowlist of current and observed bibliographic fields while ignoring blank provider values.
Normalizes equivalent text, number, identifier, and date representations before reporting differences.
Returns only differing fields with safe current/observed values and bounded authority, write-mode, lock, and same-provider context.
Shows match/difference counts and field details in Library Provider history without offering apply or rematch actions.
Extended unit, OpenAPI, BookOrbit runtime, and browser coverage for comparison behavior and internal-id exclusion.

releases.title: collectZ v3.29.6
releases.summary: Preserves the upstream metadata provider explicitly selected by BookOrbit, together with that provider's record id, without guessing from the other identifiers BookOrbit knows about.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added an optional BookOrbit native response contract at `metadataSource.provider` and `metadataSource.providerItemId`.
Accepts attribution only when both values are present, the provider is supported, and the selected id exactly matches the provider's entry in `providerIds`.
Keeps native metadata enrichment compatible when attribution is missing or inconsistent while refusing to claim a selected provider.
Preserves verified attribution in BookOrbit compatibility fields and immutable provider-observation facts.
Shows the selected metadata source separately from BookOrbit's complete provider-identifier list in Library Provider history.
Extended BookOrbit unit, transport, authoritative import, API contract, and browser coverage.

releases.title: collectZ v3.29.5
releases.summary: Makes immutable BookOrbit and Kavita source evidence safely readable through the media API and Library item drawer without exposing credentials, raw provider responses, or internal authorization state.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added a newest-first, paginated provider-observation endpoint for media records in the active workspace/library scope.

Readback includes the safe Provider Connection label/type, identity kind and lifecycle, canonical public UUID at observation time, normalized provider facts, timestamps, and stable content fingerprint.
BookOrbit history exposes normalized native/OPDS facts and upstream provider identifiers such as ComicVine or Goodreads ids when observed.
Kavita history preserves separate series/chapter evidence and safe CollectZ cover-proxy provenance.
Added a bounded Provider history section to the Library item drawer.
The projection omits workspace and actor implementation ids, identity database ids, idempotency keys, Provider Connection endpoints/settings, credentials, authorization values, and raw payloads.

releases.title: collectZ v3.29.4
releases.summary: Makes Kavita the second immutable provider-observation adopter, preserving separate series and chapter provenance without storing credentials or direct server URLs.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added an explicit Kavita normalized-fact builder at the existing immutable observation seam.
Kavita series and chapter reconciliation now appends `kavita_api` observations in the same authorized transaction as identity, canonical-field, compatibility, format, and normalized-metadata work.
Observations preserve separate Kavita series/chapter identities, library and bibliographic facts, chapter-fan-out detail, and safe CollectZ cover-proxy paths.
Queued imports derive their observation batch from the existing inline job id; synchronous imports mint one batch per request.
Exact retries within one batch reuse the observation, while later import requests append immutable history.
Kavita observation facts omit API keys, bearer tokens, raw API payloads, direct server/reader/cover URLs, and server filenames.

releases.title: collectZ v3.29.3
releases.summary: Adds an append-only, workspace-owned ledger of normalized provider facts and makes BookOrbit its first transactional adopter.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Added immutable provider source observations tied to one workspace, Provider Connection, external media identity, and observed canonical public UUID.
Added source kind, schema version, source and observation timestamps, content hashing, and import-batch idempotency without persisting raw provider payloads.

BookOrbit now records normalized OPDS or native bibliographic facts, upstream provider identifiers, ordered series memberships, and cover provenance in the same authorized transaction as canonical reconciliation.
Retrying the same durable job with unchanged facts reuses its observation; a later batch or changed normalized facts appends new history.
Database triggers reject observation updates and deletes, RLS hides rows without an authorized workspace transaction, and same-workspace foreign keys prevent identity/connection crossover.

The BookOrbit runtime smoke now proves normalized persistence, idempotency, immutability, RLS isolation, and credential-free observation facts alongside the existing identity, metadata, cover, scheduler, and series checks.

releases.title: collectZ v3.29.2
releases.summary: Makes scheduled BookOrbit target advancement and durable job creation one atomic workspace-authorized operation.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Scheduled provider enqueue now locks and rechecks the due target inside the owning transaction.
The same transaction creates or reuses the durable job and advances the target's `last_enqueued_at` timestamp.
Workspace, library, provider connection, provider type, and actor ownership are derived from the locked target and authorized scheduler context rather than copied from the caller.
A concurrent or repeated sweep sees the target as no longer due after the first committed enqueue and cannot create a second job for the cadence window.
The BookOrbit authoritative import smoke proves failed-enqueue rollback, same-transaction writes, concurrent-sweep exclusion, successful worker processing, cadence reuse, and secret-free payloads.

releases.title: collectZ v3.29.1
releases.summary: Makes Movies and Games heading counts authoritative and immediately consistent after deletion while preserving collection cards in their aggregate library views.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Aggregate Movies and Games counts now add the server-reported media total to the server-reported collection total instead of counting only collection rows loaded on the current page.
The heading count is withheld while its required media and collection result generations are unsettled, avoiding transient mixed-search totals.
Collection requests use sequencing so a slower response from an older search cannot overwrite the active result set or count.
Successful single deletion now updates media total, total pages, current page, and `hasMore` with the same shared pagination logic used by bulk deletion.
Server-backed Library pages clamp when deletion or filtering removes the final result from the last page.
Focused unit and browser coverage proves aggregate count composition, immediate deletion delta, reload persistence, stale-response rejection, and exact-title absence.

releases.title: collectZ v3.29.0
releases.summary: Makes the append-only migration chain the sole authoritative path for fresh installation, retained upgrade, restored runtime, Core startup, and Platform startup, then retires the hand-maintained duplicate schema.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Expanded fresh-install certification across relations, columns, indexes, constraints, triggers, functions, row-level security objects, migration rows, feature flags, and required bootstrap rows.

Certified exact non-owner runtime and broker role attributes, memberships, database/schema/table/sequence/function grants, default privileges, and broker mappings through a redacted provisioning inventory.

Added hosted Core evidence proving the database was empty before migration startup and that the production backend runs through a non-owner credential in external migration mode after every migration is applied.

Added restored-runtime authority evidence for database-native snapshots of migration-built databases, including exact retained counts, complete migration history, required bootstrap state, and non-owner runtime behavior.

Added contained Platform certification that starts a production-mode control-plane backend from an empty migration-built scratch database inside the canonical stack and passes the complete edition boundary.

Retired `init.sql` after the migration-built Core, Platform, retained-upgrade, restore, bootstrap, and ownership contracts were certified. The compatibility-named parity artifact now fails if that duplicate schema source reappears.
Moved workspace-ownership table discovery from duplicate-schema parsing to a direct comparison between reviewed classifications and the live migration-built PostgreSQL catalog.

releases.title: collectZ v3.28.2
releases.summary: Expands PostgreSQL row-level security across five workspace-owned operational families, including durable sync jobs, while preserving application authorization through explicit actor and narrowly bounded worker transaction grants.

details.heading: Highlights
bullets: Protected Dashboard review decisions, merge-recommendation feedback, event exclusive sources, and object relationships with ownership backfills, same-scope constraints, immutable ownership, guarded cascades, and command-appropriate policies.
Added a private transaction-scope broker for short-lived actor grants and bounded worker grants separated by claim, recovery, lifecycle, observation, maintenance, and exact-scope ingestion actions.

Moved durable enqueue, operator readback and cancellation, dashboard/activity readback, metrics observation, startup maintenance, Plex webhook ingestion and processing, valuation refresh, Plex reconciliation preview, and legacy inline-import paths behind their respective authorization contracts.
Activated command-separated `sync_jobs` policies for actor SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and worker SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE while deliberately leaving worker DELETE unavailable.

Preserved terminal job history, including null-library tombstones, without inventing ownership; migration `144` aborts on missing workspaces or cross-workspace libraries rather than rewriting ambiguous retained rows.
Added fresh-database, retained-upgrade, non-owner runtime, migration/restore, RBAC, browser, workspace-isolation, worker-action, and fixture-cleanup certification for the protected families.
